notes: The manual's pictures are dark, so exact stud positions are inferred. Most brick-on-brick joins have null ports.

Base: the two 4x10 plates sit side by side. The 1x8 tiles form a frame on them. The two gray 4x6 plates sit inside the frame across the seam. The four gray 1x6 tiles ring those plates. Interior plate/jumper/tile placement is approximate. Those pieces fill the 4x6 interior exactly (24 studs).

Tower body: layers alternate 1x3 and 2x3 bricks side by side (3x3 footprint, 9 layers in total: step 6, step 7 and the seven pairs in step 8). Each layer is joined to the one below with three edges: 2x3-on-2x3, 2x3-on-1x3 and 1x3-on-2x3.
The first 1x3 and 2x3 layer is attached to the six jumper plates (3 each) as a best guess.
The curved brick sits on the 2x2 plate from step 6, which sits on the step 5 2x2 plate.

The upper setbacks (steps 9-16) are inferred: each corner brick sits on a 2x2 brick, with a 1x1 tile on the exposed stud. The 1x1 bricks and 1x3 brick are stacked as two short columns and one tall column. The 1x2 bricks carry the two antennas.
The 3030 plate's anti-stud ports are not listed in the catalogue, so joins to it use null ports.
